portion_doctrine: Segments 1-10 of 'last lightroom hopefully.docx' comprise ~8 Lightroom portrait editing video transcripts (Zac Watson, Mark McGee, TK North, Matthew Ruderman, and others). Content is 95% operational tutorial: specific slider names, mask workflows, brush techniques, and concrete editing sequences. Boilerplate includes video intros/outros, sponsor segments, and UI navigation chatter. The real gold is repeatable Lightroom workflows and technique patterns across multiple educators.
operating_rules: Always nail white balance first (auto-correct, dropper tool, or manual temp/tint adjustment)
Decrease saturation while increasing vibrance for natural skin tones that retain pop
Apply presets to all images in a shoot, then sync (uncheck white balance and exposure when syncing)
Use radial gradients (feather at 100) to apply localized exposure/contrast shifts, not global vignette
Invert radial masks to darken/desaturate background while keeping subject bright
Reduce texture and clarity (-8 to -10) on skin masks for subtle airbrush effect without Vaseline look
Keep eye retouching subtle: never push clarity too far on eyes or they look scary and unnatural
Use brush masks with low flow (for blending) and hold Alt/Option to erase/minus overexposed areas
Masking workflow: Select People first to auto-detect facial skin, body skin, hair, clothes; create individual masks per category
Use Heal/Remove tool with generative AI for blemishes and distractions (stack multiple removes in same generation)
Set opacity to 50-60% for under-eye bags/creases; 100% for pimples/spots
Crop to rule-of-thirds early; use Alt+Shift to crop from inside out
Export at 5MB for social, 10MB for portraits; always use sRGB color space
Create dark moody portraits by: global exposure -3 to -4 stops, increase highlights to 100%, raise shadows +20-30%, use curves white-point drag for contrast
For catch lights in eyes: create hard-edge brush mask over catch light, drag curves white point in, subtract unwanted section with soft brush
named_methods: Five Lightroom Portrait Tips (Zac Watson): white balance, skin flattening (clarity/texture drop), masking workflow, eye enhancement, vignetting
Editing Workflow (Matthew Ruderman): preset sync with white balance/exposure unchecked, tone curve S-curve, cropping, point color tool, retouching with heel tool (50-60% opacity)
Dark Moody Portraits (Mark McGee): background mask with curves white-point drag, person masks for contrast/eye sparkle, brush masks for shard-of-light effect, object selection for color accents

Five Portrait Enhancement Tips (TK North): fix skin tones (HSL color selector), smooth skin (clarity/texture reduction via brush), blemish/tired-eye removal (spot removal), eye enhancement (iris enhance preset), radial filters to draw eye to subject

Culling via Narrative: scenes view (auto-groups similar framing), AI first-pass filter (potential/unlikely/undesirable), face analysis mode (zoom on eyes, focus rating 1-10), rate 1-star in keyboard, target 50-60 keepers per portrait session

General Editing Sequence: culling (Narrative) -> preset apply -> white balance adjust -> exposure/tone curve -> masking (select subject, invert for background) -> individual masks (hair contrast boost, clothes, skin, eyes) -> brush masks (eye brightening, blemish removal) -> export settings
Point Color Tool: eyedropper selects any color in image, adjust hue/saturation/luminance independently; careful as it affects all instances of that color
Retouching Method 1 (Heel Tool): set opacity 50-60% for creases/bags, 100% for spots/pimples; avoid eyelashes; adjust source area to bottom of panel
Retouching Method 2 (Mask + Clarity): select facial skin + body skin via people mask, reduce texture -8 to -10 and clarity slightly for airbrush glow

Eye Enhancement Multi-Step: (1) brush mask, increase exposure + color temp warmth, (2) iris enhance preset (or manual exposure/clarity/saturation boost), (3) hard-edge catch-light mask with curves adjustment, (4) whites enhancement (shadows +50%, desaturate reds), (5) hold Alt to erase overexposed areas

content_ideas: Hierarchy of Lightroom adjustments: white balance first, then exposure/tone curve, then masking, then localized brush work (eye/blemish)
Skin tone truth: HSL color selector tool (click and drag on image) > manual hue/saturation sliders, because it self-targets the exact color you clicked
Radial gradient masterclass: feather 100, invert to affect everything outside subject, moveable unlike vignette in effects tab
Brush mask parameters matter: size + feather + flow + density all independently control how aggressive the edit feels; low flow = blendable, high density = full effect to edges
Eye editing is the 80/20 of portrait impact: exposure boost + color temp warmth + iris texture + whites desaturation + catch-light precision = portrait transforms
Culling tool psychology: Narrative's scenes view + AI first-pass filter + face focus rating saves 30-50% of time vs manual grid scroll
Dark moody portraits don't need fancy plugins: curves white-point drag + background/person masks + optional shard-of-light brush = professional result
Generative remove tool stacks edits: don't click-generate-click-generate; paint all distractions, then generate once
Preset as starting point, not destination: always sync with white balance/exposure unchecked, always adjust per-image
gates: White balance gate: always fix first, before any other adjustment, because wrong WB cascades into HSL color work
Preset sync gate: always uncheck white balance and exposure when syncing presets across a batch (light changes between shots)
Masking prioritization gate: do global adjustments (exposure/tone curve) first, then masks, then brush work; inverse order leads to fighting each other
Eye subtlety gate: if eyes look scary or unnatural after enhancement, they've been over-edited; pull back significantly
Retouching opacity gate: 50-60% for texture softening, 100% for spot removal; no middle ground, each has different purpose
contradictions: Texture reduction for skin softening (Zac Watson -8 to -10) vs texture increase for eye detail (TK North + clarity for iris) - both true, context-dependent: skin = reduction, eye iris/lashes = increase

Saturation reducer vs HSL saturation boost - saturation slider affects all colors equally (bad for skin), HSL selector lets you target one color (good for skin); use HSL for skin, saturation for global/background
Spot removal opacity 50% for tired eyes vs 100% for pimples - both stated as gospel, same tool, different opacity settings based on desired invisibility (bags=blend, spots=erase)
weird_gold: Narrative's 'scenes view' (press S in grid) auto-groups nearly-identical shots by framing, saves 300+ of 900 photos instantly when combined with AI first-pass filter
The 'scrella' mispronunciation arc (sclera = white of eye, iris = colored part) - Zac Watson hesitates, doesn't know if he said it right, keeps going; it's right
Matthew Ruderman's D700 camera profile switch (D700 shot looks colder than Z9, camera standard profile makes it yellow, Adobe Color keeps consistency across 4+ different camera bodies in one shoot)
TK North's grain bonus tip: dial up grain amount and size in Effects tab for film look; it's not noise reduction, it's intentional texture add
Mark McGee's shard-of-light technique: feathered brush mask at 40%, hold Shift to draw straight line of light across dark portrait, moveable, creates dramatic three-point lighting effect

The catch-light precision dance: hard-edge brush over catch light, drag curves white point in to see what you're doing, subtract with soft brush to leave only the specular highlight (pure white), then manipulate curves to blend naturally into surrounding eye detail
Face analysis mode in Narrative (press / in grid): automatically detects every face, zooms on eyes, rates focus 1-10 with colored dots; works on group photos with 6+ people, each gets its own zoom
Alt+Shift in crop tool drags from inside-out instead of corner-out; minor UX pattern but reveals Lightroom respects two-handed gesture logic
